picks.title: YouTube explains its AI slop policy and why some creators won't get paid
picks.excerpt: YouTube spelled out which AI-made video stops earning money: generic mass-produced clips, repetitive templates and fake personas dispensing serious advice. The rules redraw the line between AI-assisted craft and AI-generated filler for anyone shipping video at volume.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the most directly actionable: YouTube's own wording on what AI video still monetizes changes what creators publish tomorrow.

picks.title: NVIDIA tackles deepfakes and opens the door to AI agents at SIGGRAPH 2026
picks.excerpt: NVIDIA introduced a synthetic video detector aimed at newsrooms and broadcasters at SIGGRAPH 2026, analysing footage frame-by-frame with up to 92% accuracy on uncompressed video. The same announcement opens NVIDIA tooling to MCP-driven AI agents inside production software.
picks.rationale: Two shifts in one release — verification of synthetic footage, and MCP agents reaching into the production apps artists already run. Distinct from the previously published Cosmos 3 Super item.

picks.title: This New Tool Aims to Be Able to Identify and Trace AI Videos Back to Their Sources
picks.excerpt: UC Riverside researchers built SAGA, a forensic framework that reads the fingerprints a generator leaves in frame-to-frame variation. It aims to answer not just whether a clip is AI, but which model made it.
picks.rationale: Attribution, not just detection — naming the model behind a clip is what provenance and rights disputes actually need, and it comes from published research rather than a vendor claim.

picks.title: Practice Makes Magic: The Human Hands Behind ChikaBOOM!
picks.excerpt: Director c. Craig walks through the hand-made animation of Tribeca short ChikaBOOM! and pushes back on calling generative work 'artificial'. His argument: generative tools only hold up when the craft and labour behind them are visible.
picks.rationale: A working director's account of where generative tools earn their place in an animation pipeline — the craft counterweight to the week's policy and detection stories.

picks.title: From Script to $100K Equity Financing: Navigating The Greenlight List
picks.excerpt: A look at AI-assisted script coverage: Greenlight Coverage scores screenplays with data science to estimate audience and distribution before a frame is shot. Development notes move from taste to model output.
picks.rationale: Moves the AI story upstream to development — a model scoring a screenplay before production changes how writers pitch and how projects get greenlit.
